method: Compare distinct allocation occurrence IDs within each stage only. FAPs and untrusted NEP primary titles excluded. Same normalized official PAP and either qualified municipality/province or same implementing office required. At least three shared distinctive nonnumeric title tokens required. Same base title after trailing geographic metadata removal, or ≥0.94 SequenceMatcher similarity with qualified municipality/province AND identical distinctive token sets, produces a candidate. Changed route-endpoint or other distinctive scope tokens veto even when text similarity is high. Direction, qualified-location and tranche conflicts veto. Explicit disjoint ranges veto. No amount-equality requirement. Missing chainage never proves scope overlap.
limits: Matching allocation occurrences does not establish duplicate contracts, duplicate payment, fraud or authorship. Different engineering components and legitimate amendments can share titles.
Office-only agreement is weaker than site evidence. Unresolved locations are never inferred from similar names.
Pair counts are not project counts: three linked records produce three pairs. Distinct occurrence counts are shown separately; amounts are not summed as loss.
Exact official PAP blocking, trusted-title requirements and conservative location rules miss possible cross-program, paraphrased or unresolved duplicates. No flag is not clearance.
Tranche differences are excluded from this conservative queue, not certified as legitimate. Missing chainage requires source and engineering-scope review.
NEP baseline includes source records outside the API. Its documented source-title confidence limits remain applicable.
